sections.html:
Conway is where Faulkner County keeps its courthouse, about 30 miles up the road from Little Rock. Interstate 40 bends around the north and east edges of the city (Conway exits run 124 through 132), and US 64 and US 65 cut across town. Russellville is 46 miles off. A lot of houses here are a few minutes from a ramp, which suits people who commute toward Little Rock.

The 2020 census put Conway at 64,134 residents, against 58,908 in 2010, and the July 2025 estimate stands at 72,328. The median age of 30.7 reflects the colleges. Expect a buyer pool heavy with first-timers, plus renters ready to buy. Houses near Lake Conway attract a different crowd than houses near the campuses.

Lake Conway on the city's edge is billed as the largest man-made lake built by a state game and fish commission anywhere in the country, so waterfront and near-water listings carry a draw that inland streets lack. The older core near the railroad, where the town began in 1872 as Conway Station, has the age and the quirks that go with it. If your house sits in either area, say so up front and gather what you know about its history and upkeep.

sections.h2: Who is buying: jobs and colleges
sections.html:
Work in Conway is spread across health care, higher education, data services and the public schools. Conway Regional Health System, the University of Central Arkansas and Acxiom top the employer list. That mix steadies demand, yet a layoff or a transfer still pushes some owners to sell on a short clock.

Three colleges shape rentals and sale timing. UCA enrolls about 12,000, Hendrix College a little over 1,300 and Central Baptist College nearly 900. Landlords around campus often put a unit up for sale right after a tenant leaves, because a vacant place with deferred repairs shows poorly in the middle of the school year. A cash buyer who accepts the house in its current state can close on that schedule. A traditional listing may have to wait for the next semester.

Most of Conway falls under Conway Public Schools, which runs 16 schools for roughly 10,000 students. A few pockets belong to the Mayflower and Greenbrier districts, so look up the exact address before you tell a buyer which schools apply. Conway Christian School and St. Joseph Catholic School are the larger private choices.

Annual rainfall runs near 51 inches, and snow is uncommon. That puts the load on roofs, gutters, crawlspaces and cooling systems. When an air conditioner or heat pump is nearly worn out, a buyer's inspector will point at it early. Owners of older roofs should hold on to storm-damage paperwork, since buyers and lenders request it.

  • Write down the roof's age and any hail or wind claims.
  • Check beneath the floor for damp after a wet spring.
  • Pull out your HVAC service records.

sections.h2: Due dates and penalties for property tax
sections.html:
Tax ruleWhat applies in Faulkner County
Payment windowMarch 1 to October 15
Late penalty on real estate tax10%
Interest after October 1510% a year
Homestead creditUp to $600 a year

Stop by the collector at 806 Faulkner St. in Conway between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, or use the Greenbrier branch. You can pay by mail, online or at the counter. One quirk: the personal property bill (a vehicle, for example) has to be settled first or alongside the real estate bill, and an unpaid vehicle charge can lock you out of paying the real estate bill online.

If you live in the house, you apply for the homestead credit one time, and you apply again if you move. When the sale closes, the title company usually divides that year's tax between you and the buyer. Request the numbers early and verify them with the collector. State law sets the payment window in Ark. Code 26-36-201.

You can sell with tax unpaid; the balance simply comes out of your proceeds at the closing table and keeps growing with penalty and interest until then. Phone the collector for a payoff amount before weighing offers. An estate debt or a lien works the same way, so the title company will want payoff figures for each. Collect them at the start so nothing surprises you in the last week.

The state adds a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of the actual price whenever a deed conveys real estate. The Department of Finance and Administration runs it, and the stamp is purchased at recording. Whoever pays is decided in your contract. Faulkner County deeds are recorded through the circuit clerk, whose office offers an online land records search.

  • An agent listing: commission, repairs the buyer requests after inspection, and months of carrying costs if the house lingers.
  • A sale by owner: your own money for marketing and legal forms, and your own evenings for showings.
  • A cash offer: no repair requests, because the buyer takes the house as is, and a closing date written into the contract.

Four situations come up most: an inherited house with nobody to live in it, a rental trashed by the last tenant, a job move, or a mortgage that slipped behind. Each carries its own deadline.

With an inherited house, the estate paperwork has to be in order before a deed can be signed, and that goes through the court. With a rental, settle the tenant question first, because an occupied house narrows what a buyer can do. If you owe taxes or face a lien, get the payoff figures.

Start with a written list covering who is on the title, what is owed, how the roof and systems look, and the date you need to be done. A cash buyer can quote from that sheet, and you can set the quote beside what a listing would leave you after commission and repairs.

After you accept an offer, the title company confirms who owns the house and what is owed against it, then builds the settlement statement. On that statement the year's tax is prorated, any mortgage is paid off and the transfer tax is settled. A buyer paying cash needs no loan approval or lender appraisal, so timing rests mostly on the title work. With a listing, showings, financing and an appraisal all add days. In both cases the title company sets the closing date.

Bring a photo ID, the deed or estate documents, and your payoff letter. Every owner named on the title has to sign, which is the step that slows many family sales.

faqs.q: How long does a house take to sell in Conway?
faqs.a: That depends on how you sell. A cash deal can close once the title work is finished, while a listing adds showings, financing and an appraisal.

faqs.q: When are Faulkner County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax can be paid from March 1 through October 15. Later payments pick up a 10% penalty and 10% annual interest.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when I sell in Conway?
faqs.a: Yes, the state charges $3.30 per $1,000 of the actual price on a deed that conveys real estate. The contract decides which side pays.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Conway house with a tenant in it?
faqs.a: Yes, though the buyer inherits the lease. Mention the lease terms and rent to any buyer early, since they affect price and timing.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Conway house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No, a cash buyer builds the condition into the price. Compare that figure with what a repaired listing would net after costs.
